title: The salmon
logline: Wednesday. The cedar-plank salmon, analyzed. The cedar. Wood draws the plank's grain and the strip, without saying it, draws the mill's cedar. Gully notices what the strip won't say.

panels.composition: Gully's. WOOD drawing. The pad: a cedar plank, the salmon on it, the grain drawn with real attention.

balloons.text: Cedar plank. Western red. Soaked two hours — they said two; it was ninety minutes, you could tell by the char —

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a thin man on a stool drawing a cedar plank with a salmon on it, the wood grain rendered with unusual care, a man in an apron and an old dog in a basket

panels.composition: The plank's grain, close. The rings. Old growth. The mill's cedar, if anyone's counting.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, close-up of an ink drawing of cedar wood grain with tight old-growth rings
image.notes: The mill's cedar. The strip never says it; Gully does, sideways.

panels.composition: Gully, looking at the grain on the pad. Knowing the grain.

balloons.text: That's old growth, Woody. That's ours. Somebody up there's cooking fish on our —

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a stocky man in an apron looking closely at a drawing of wood grain and recognizing it

panels.composition: The two of them looking at the drawing of a plank. The dog. The salmon, incidental. The strip about the wood.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, two men looking down at a drawing of a cedar plank on a pad, an old dog in a basket between them, no words

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: The plank's grain is the mill's. 'That's ours.'
